explanation: Layer-0 context-free token detector: the positive pole's strength is a fixed lookup on the current token id alone (the same value at any position, in prose, code, tables or any language), so it fires exactly when the text contains one of its tokens, strongest on the word 'post' itself ('Post' 1.37, ' post' 1.25, 'post' 1.15, ' Post' 0.89) and on whole 'post-...' compound tokens (' postoperatively' 0.90, ' posted' 0.88, ' posting' 0.88, ' posts' 0.80, ' Postal' 0.79, ' postpartum' 0.67, 'POST' 0.66, ' postoperative' 0.54, ' postal' 0.53, ' postnatal' 0.42); because the tokenizer keeps most 'post...' words as a ' post'/'Post' token plus a second token (postmaster, postcard, postscript, postgraduate, postcode, post-apocalyptic, postpone), those fire through that first token too, whereas whole tokens that merely contain the letters post (' poster' 0.11, ' posters' 0.11, ' postseason' 0.24, ' posture' 0.23, ' postponed' 0.20, ' posterior' -0.17, ' postulated' -0.16, ' compost' -0.06) stay below the 0.25x max = 0.343 active line. A weaker second cluster covers some time nouns (' Week' 1.22, 'time' 0.82, ' Day' 0.79, ' Era' 0.78, ' era' 0.69, ' time' 0.68, ' Time' 0.60, ' times' 0.57, but not ' days', ' weeks', ' months', ' years', ' Monday', ' morning', ' hour', ' minute' or 'today', which separates it from the sister time-unit neuron N1101+), the prefix tokens 'pre' 1.09, ' pret' 1.02, ' Pret' 0.97, ' pre' 0.88 (while ' prevent', ' previous', 'president', ' press' are at or below 0), and an otherwise unstructured tail of about 3,400 vocabulary types that share its embedding direction ('è' 1.03, 'arr' 0.93, 'table' 0.93, 'é' 0.91, 'text' 0.90, ' household' 0.85, ' made' 0.82, ' garden' 0.52, ' trip' 0.47); that tail puts roughly 2% of mixed-corpus tokens over the active line, so ordinary function words stay near zero but about one word in fifty of ordinary text still trips the pole with no 'post' present.
